Swift enum descriptor 0x347c declares 11 payload and 13 empty cases; field descriptor 0x3880 agrees. Outer enum descriptor 0x3498 and its ABI-declared cached singleton accessor 0x179c establish the metadata passed to the exact libswiftCore runtime tag call at 0x1498. Every incoming path to the outlined getter is dominated by that call and selects outer tag 0; reflection field 0x39c0 directly references fixed enum descriptor 0x347c. Its static enum metadata 0x4218 points back to that descriptor and declares value-witness table 0x4198, value size 156 and complete straight-line getEnumTag function 0x23b4. On every path the unchanged incoming outer object is copied at offset zero by the exact libSystem memcpy import into a fixed private frame interval of that size; no intervening unknown call or overlapping write is admitted. The getter called at 0x14f0 targets 0x17fc, either that declared getter or an equal complete straight-line body, and reads only that interval. Shared helper code never supplies enum identity or count. Its unchanged tag reaches the LDRSW index after an explicit 32-bit zero-extending write. Signed 32-bit entries at 0x173c are added to 0x150c. REA+ restored computed edges, disassembled destinations and extended the owning function before observations; generated override labels are analysis metadata, not source/caller declarations.

limitations: Case values are Swift ABI runtime tags, with payload cases before empty cases; field names are reflection metadata. Valid enum values supply the bound; this does not establish state reachability or original source order.
Control-flow recovery assumes the normal AArch64 ABI and private non-escaped frame storage. It does not execute the target or prove each case's high-level semantics.
Types and calling conventions are Ghidra decompiler observations, not source declarations.
Register variables, compiler-generated blocks, and pointer arithmetic remain decompiler artifacts.
Pseudocode is neither original source nor guaranteed to compile.

On supported non-Windows AArch64 Mach-O inputs, REA+ can restore signed-word Swift enum dispatches from verified ABI metadata, accessor and instruction flow. Generated switch overrides are analysis metadata. Recovery budgets are 4096 cases, 100000 CFG/reaching-definition work units per candidate function and 256 nested queries; unsupported or exhausted paths remain unrecovered, not complete.

limitations: High p-code is decompiler-derived, not original source or runtime behavior. is_dead preserves the Java AST flag; decoded block members can retain that flag, so block_membership separately reports actual syntax-tree membership.
Def-use links do not cross function boundaries and may omit memory aliasing, call side effects, or unresolved indirect flow.
Memory read/write effects include stack and temporary memory operations; they do not identify persistent state or business meaning.
Operation, input, and def-use limits can truncate large functions; inspect truncation, omitted lower bounds, and known omitted counts before drawing conclusions.
Known omitted-edge counts cover links omitted from retained operations; omitted operations may contain additional uncounted links.
Unresolved computed or indirect flows without target addresses are not represented as reference edges.
Thunk and external classifications are Ghidra FunctionManager observations; they do not resolve targetless calls.
Pseudocode and assembly are Ghidra-specific representations, not original source or Hopper-equivalent text.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
References cover the complete Ghidra function-body AddressSet and exact entry. Dossier incoming edges omit sources owned by that function; procedure_references also retains those internal edges.
The dossier combines Ghidra FunctionManager, Listing, ReferenceManager, BasicBlockModel, and decompiler observations; provider-specific pseudocode and assembly are not cross-provider text invariants.

Resolved reference metadata identifies computed, indirect, external, call, jump, and data edges; unresolved targetless flows remain unknown, and function classifications distinguish thunks and externals.
Synthetic Ghidra entry-point references without actionable memory sources are omitted.
The Java bridge serializes one function request per Program and lets each decompilation run until it completes or the caller cancels.
